title: The Post-Election Tally: Inside the Remaining Uncalled Midterm Battles
snippet: While Democrats have swept to decisive majorities in the House, Senate, and statehouses nationwide, several high-profile races—including key Senate seats and Rep. Lauren Boebert's reelection fight—remain unsettled.
content:
WASHINGTON — The dust has largely settled on a sweeping Democratic victory in the 2026 midterm elections, but election workers across the country are still hard at work finalizing results in a handful of high-stakes, razor-thin contests.

Democrats have already locked in control of Capitol Hill and broadened their footprint in state capitals nationwide, scoring historic pickups in deep-red territory. Yet key battles—spanning Senate showdowns in Mississippi and Alaska to high-profile House races across the Sun Belt—remain officially unresolved.

The Battle for the Senate: Expanding the Majority

Heading into Election Day, Democrats needed a net gain of four seats to retake the Senate. They easily cleared that bar, defending competitive seats in Michigan, Georgia, Minnesota, and New Hampshire while flipping seven GOP-held seats in Maine, Texas, South Carolina, Ohio, North Carolina, Iowa, and Kansas. Only two high-profile Republican incumbents—Florida's Ashley Moody and Nebraska's Pete Ricketts—managed to hold their seats.

Democrats will enter the 2027 legislative session holding at least 54 Senate seats. That majority could expand to 56 depending on two lingering contests:

  • Mississippi: Democratic challenger Scott Colom holds a 2,536-vote lead over Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith as remaining absentee ballots trickle in. Though 97% of votes are counted, the narrow 0.27% margin has kept news outlets from officially calling the race.
  • Alaska: Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan by 637 votes with 74% of the vote counted. Due to Alaska's ranked-choice voting rules, if neither candidate tops 50% of first-choice votes, the state will begin counting secondary preferences on Nov. 18.

House Races: Boebert Trails as Count Nears Conclusion

In the House of Representatives, Democrats have already secured 254 seats—well past the 218 needed for a majority—driven by a 13-point national popular vote margin. However, 20 contests remain outstanding.

The most closely watched unresolved House race is in Colorado's 4th Congressional District, where conservative firebrand Rep. Lauren Boebert trails Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral, by more than 3,000 votes with just 2% of ballots remaining to be tallied.

Other unresolved House contests include runoff matches in Louisiana, high-margin counts in California, and tight races in Florida, Minnesota, and North Carolina.

Gubernatorial and Statehouse Surges

Democrats also broke a 15-year streak of Republican gubernatorial dominance, flipping state executive offices in Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Nevada, and Georgia to claim 29 governorships nationwide. In Kansas, Democrat Cindy Holscher holds a lead of more than 7,500 votes over Republican Ty Masterson as counties prepare to finalize their statutory audits.

Down-ballot, Democrats flipped over 500 state legislative seats and flipped 12 legislative chambers blue, picking up full state government 'trifectas' in states like Arizona and Wisconsin.
